title: Lint: unused and unsorted imports
body: Ruff reports unused imports in money.py and formats.py, and unsorted imports in invoice.py and formats.py. Clean them up. Nothing else should change.

tests.tests/test_t01.py:
import subprocess
import sys


def test_lint():
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "ruff", *"check --isolated --select E,F,I --line-length 100 ledgerline".split()], capture_output=True, text=True
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr

title: Docstrings for money.py
body: The public functions in money.py (to_money, format_amount, percent_of) have no docstrings. Add a short docstring to each saying what it returns.

title: Type hints for dates.py
body: Add type hints to every function in dates.py: dates are datetime.date, terms_days is an int, days_overdue returns an int and is_overdue returns a bool.

title: days_overdue goes negative
body: dates.days_overdue returns a negative number of days before the due date. It should return 0 until the invoice is overdue.

tests.tests/test_t05.py:
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from ledgerline import dates


def test_not_negative():
    assert dates.days_overdue(date(2026, 3, 10), date(2026, 3, 1)) == 0
    assert dates.days_overdue(date(2026, 3, 10), date(2026, 3, 10)) == 0
    assert dates.days_overdue(date(2026, 3, 10), date(2026, 3, 13)) == 3

title: Discounted lines ignore the quantity
body: A line with a discount is charged as if its quantity were 1. Three items at 10.00 with 10% off should come to 27.00, not 9.00.

title: Discount on the whole invoice
body: Add Invoice.apply_discount(percent) for a discount on the whole invoice. It comes off the subtotal, and tax is worked out on what's left. Refuse a percent below 0 or above 100 with ValueError.

tests.tests/test_t07.py:
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from ledgerline.invoice import Invoice, Line


def test_invoice_discount():
    invoice = Invoice("INV-7", date(2026, 3, 2))
    invoice.add_line(Line("Service", 1, Decimal("100.00")))
    invoice.apply_discount(Decimal("10"))
    assert invoice.subtotal() == Decimal("90.00")
    assert invoice.tax() == Decimal("18.00")
    assert invoice.total() == Decimal("108.00")
    for bad in (-1, 101):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            invoice.apply_discount(Decimal(bad))

title: CSV export breaks on commas
body: to_csv writes descriptions as they are, so a description with a comma or a quote breaks the row. Quote fields properly.

tests.tests/test_t08.py:
import csv
import io
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from ledgerline import formats
from ledgerline.invoice import Invoice, Line


def test_commas_and_quotes():
    invoice = Invoice("INV-8", date(2026, 3, 2))
    invoice.add_line(Line('Paint, white "matt"', 2, Decimal("4.50")))
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(formats.to_csv(invoice))))
    assert rows[1][:4] == ['Paint, white "matt"', "2", "4.50", "9.00"]

title: Tax is a cent off
body: Our accountant says tax is sometimes a cent off. Tax must be worked out once, on the invoice subtotal, and rounded half up to the cent: not per line, and not in floats.

tests.tests/test_t09.py:
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from ledgerline.invoice import Invoice, Line


def test_tax_on_subtotal():
    invoice = Invoice("INV-9", date(2026, 3, 2), tax_rate=Decimal("0.07"))
    for _ in range(3):
        invoice.add_line(Line("Stamp", 1, Decimal("0.50")))
    assert invoice.tax() == Decimal("0.11")
    assert invoice.total() == Decimal("1.61")

title: Support invoices in other currencies
body: We're starting to bill customers abroad, so invoices need a currency. Give Invoice and Line a currency code (default EUR). An invoice must refuse a line in another currency with ValueError. format_amount should take an optional currency and show it before the amount, like "USD 1,234.50", and the CSV export needs a currency column at the end.

tests.tests/test_t11.py:
import csv
import io
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from ledgerline import formats, money
from ledgerline.invoice import Invoice, Line


def test_currency():
    assert money.format_amount(1234.5, "USD") == "USD 1,234.50"
    assert money.format_amount(1234.5) == "1,234.50"
    invoice = Invoice("INV-11", date(2026, 3, 2), currency="USD")
    invoice.add_line(Line("Widget", 2, Decimal("4.50"), currency="USD"))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        invoice.add_line(Line("Widget", 1, Decimal("4.50"), currency="GBP"))
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(formats.to_csv(invoice))))
    assert rows[0][-1] == "currency"
    assert rows[1][-1] == "USD"
    assert Invoice("INV-12", date(2026, 3, 2)).currency == "EUR"

title: Small fix: due dates on weekends
body: A due date that lands on a Saturday or Sunday should move to the next working day. Skip the public holidays in holidays.py too.

tests.tests/test_t12.py:
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from ledgerline import dates
from ledgerline.invoice import Invoice


def test_weekend_and_holidays():
    assert dates.due_date(date(2026, 3, 4), 10) == date(2026, 3, 16)
    assert dates.due_date(date(2026, 12, 16), 10) == date(2026, 12, 29)
    assert dates.due_date(date(2025, 12, 2), 30) == date(2026, 1, 2)
    assert dates.due_date(date(2026, 3, 2), 30) == date(2026, 4, 1)
    invoice = Invoice("INV-12", date(2026, 12, 16), terms_days=10)
    assert invoice.due == date(2026, 12, 29)
